newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOKYO ALUMINIUM FUTURES END DOWN ON DOLLAR MOVES.
newsitem.headline: TOKYO ALUMINIUM FUTURES END DOWN ON DOLLAR MOVES.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures finished mostly lower on Tuesday as worries over the dollar's recent fluctuations prompted stop-loss selling, traders said.
"The dollar's recovering a little bit. But its fall over the weekend has rekindled worries over foreign exchange rates," said a trader at one of Japan's leading trade houses.
"People who had bought contracts above 200 yen are now squaring their positions," he added.
The dollar was trading at just above 116 yen on Tuesday afternoon, down from around 115 yen on Monday but well below the level of 118 yen seen late last week.
The June contract ended 0.2 yen lower at 197.6 yen per kilo and the April lost 0.2 to 199.0 yen. Others were between 0.1 yen higher to 1.0 yen lower. The estimated volume was 4,449 lots.
In London overnight, the three month aluminium shrugged off a rise in June IPAI producer inventories, finishing up $4 at $1,750 per tonne. -- Tokyo Commodities Desk +81-3-3432-6179
